page.layout: One page of running text, full width, single column. No marginal notes. Small bullet marks sit in the left margin beside several lines; these are printer's marks, not notes, and are left out. Catchword at lower right.

main_text.p: cum legitur Evangelium, sedere cum praelegitur epistola, genuflectere cum Decalogus: Quam frequentem oportet esse libri revolutionem à Psalmis ad collectas, ab iis ad hymnos, inde ad Psalmos, ad lectiones, ad Litaniam. §. Exotica prorsus phraseologia Papismum redolet; etenim plurimas habet voces Scotis penitus barbaras à Romanis factis omnes mutuatas: v. g. Manutinas, vespertinas, Adventum, Epiphaniam, septuagesimam, sexagesimam, quinquagesimam, Dominicam, rogationes, loci ordinarium, collectas, litanias, Venite, Te Deum, Benedictum, Magnificat, Nunc dimittis, sabbatum cantate, Dies cinerum, oblationes, antiphonias, puerperarum purificatio. Actorum Apostolicorum & Prophetarum veteris testamenti capita quaedam dicuntur Epistolae, offertorium, Annunciatio Domine nostrae, officiare, corporale, utraque species, & cæt. Insolitæ &c exoticæ hæ voces, quibus perstringuntur populi aures, metus haud injusti anfam præbet, ne sublatinorum illorum verborum involucro late-antur etiam Sacra Latina. 6. In Calendario, sanctorum numero asscribuntur quidam, cum, an atri fuerint an albi, ignoretur: v. g. Lucianus, Rex David, Kentigernus, Fabianus, Agneta, Vincentius, Blasius, Valertinus, Colmannus, Patricius Episcopus, Cuthbertus, Benedictus, Gilbertus, Serfius, S. Georgius, Dunstanus, Suithinus, Nomen Iesu. Æ-gidius, Ninianus, Adamannus, Sapientia, Crispinus, Hugo Episcopus, Sylvester & cæt. 7. Confessio peccatorum & absolutio ante orationem præ-legi jubetur. pag. 35. quasi vero confessio non esset precatio, & in ea, multa à Deo non peterentur. 8. Verba illa conclusoria orationis Dominicæ, quia tuum est regnum, & cæt. aliquando omitti jubentur, aliquando recitari; & cui bono? 9. Singulis diebus, Te Deum laudamus, prælegi aut cani jubetur, quasi hymnus ille ab hominibus compositus,

page.notes: The page-number and running head are printed in the top line. Section signs (§) appear inline before items 5 and 6 and are rendered as printed. Bullet marks in the left margin are omitted as printer's marks. The paragraph is a continuous run of text; no printed paragraph indents are visible, so it is kept as one paragraph continuing from the previous page. "pag. 35." is printed with a space ("3 5."); transcribed as "35.". Item numbers appear mid-line and are kept inline as printed.
